...RESPONDENTS (BY SRI. RANSA VASANTHI D.L., HCGP., FOR R1  SRI.P.V. CHANDRASHEKAR, ADVOCATE FOR R2 & R3)
 THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 &
227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA, PRAYING TO QUASH THE GENERAL AWARD BEARING NO.
SLAO/NIMZ/KIADB/TU/10615/2019-20 DTD 11.04.2019 PASSED BY RESPONDENT NO.3 IN RESPECT OF THE PETITIONERS WAS THE ABSOLUTE OWNER OF LAND BEARING SY NO. 27/5 MEASURING 1 ACRE 03 GUNTAS SITUATED AT SANGENAHALLI VILLAGE, KORA HOBLI, TUMKUR TALUK,
TUMKUR DISTRICT OF PETITIONERS IS CONCERNED WHICH IS PRODUCED AT ANNEXURE-C.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER R.DEVDAS J., (ORAL):
Learned HCGP takes notice for respondent No.1.
Learned Counsel Sri P.V.Chandrashekar, has entered appearance for respondents No.2 and 3-KIADB.

Learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that a General Award has been passed only on the ground that the petitioner was absent when the matter was heard by the Special Land Acquisition Officer for award of compensation, as could be seen in the discussions made in the General Award dated 11.04.2019 at Annexure-'C'.
3.

Learned Counsel submits that this Court has held in several matters including the recent decision in the case of Harisha.R /vs./ State of Karnataka and others in W.P.No.12703/2023 dated Sri. Doddananjaiah vs The State Of Karnataka on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112842984/
3 27.06.2023 following an earlier decision in W.P.No. 6198/2015, that the land loser would be entitled for a better price as compensation instead of determination under a General Award.

entities.text: Harisha.R /vs./ State of Karnataka and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sri. Doddananjaiah vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As a consequence, all such matters where it was found that a General Award was passed only on some technical ground that the land loser was not present at the time of hearing or such other technical reasons, this Court was of the considered opinion that since the land loser would get a better price if the compensation is awarded in terms of the NC: 2023:KHC:29299 agreement and not under a General Award, the award may be passed in terms of an agreement.
Therefore, the learned counsel submits that similar benefit should be given to the petitioners.
4. On going through the following judgments, which were rendered by this Court:

entities.text: Smt. Rukmani v/s State of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: this Court is of the considered opinion that the petitioners are entitled for similar relief as was given in the cases mentioned hereinabove.

5. Consequently, the following:
NC: 2023:KHC:29299 ORDER (i) The writ petition is allowed.
(ii) The impugned General Award dated 11.04.2019 at Annexure-C insofar as the petitioners land is concerned is set aside.

(iii) The respondent-Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB is directed to reconsider the request of the petitioners for award of compensation by way of an agreement under Section 29(2) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966 and pass necessary orders within a period of Sri. Doddananjaiah vs The State Of Karnataka on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112842984/
4 three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
(iv) The respondent - Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB, is at liberty to withdraw the amount that has been deposited by it pursuant to the General Award before the jurisdictional court.
(v) Needless to state that in the event of any dispute, the General Award would stand restored.
Ordered accordingly.
